appraisal_events.evidence: « Elle n’est pas gentille du tout, Oriane... ce n’est plus mon Oriane d’autrefois, on me l’a changée... elle ne vaut pas la peine que tu t’occupes d’elle », and later « Dans le fond Oriane ne l’aime pas parce qu’elle la sent plus intelligente ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup directly criticizes Oriane's character and dismisses her as unworthy of the narrator's attention, even suggesting she is petty toward a rival; the narrator's aside that Robert is « se trahissant naïvement » signals that this judgment reveals more about Robert's own soured feelings than an objective assessment of Oriane.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Voilà une jeune femme intelligente et qui te plairait... C'est quelqu'un de gentil, tu sais, c'est quelqu'un de bien »; she is also credited with kindness to former governesses and some Dreyfusard sympathy.
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup praises the cousine de Poictiers's intelligence, beauty, and moral delicacy, explicitly favoring her over Oriane; the narrator's note that these are newly and ardently adopted fashionable phrases of Robert's casts mild ironic distance on the depth of the endorsement.

status_effects.explanation: Saint-Loup's blame, including the insinuation that Oriane is jealous of a more intelligent rival, locally lowers her, though the narrator's framing of his naive self-betrayal tempers how reliable this diminishment is.

She is elevated by Saint-Loup's explicit, itemized praise and by being favorably compared to Oriane, though the narrator's noted fashionableness of Robert's vocabulary slightly qualifies the sincerity of that praise.

ambiguities: The narrator flags that Saint-Loup is 'se trahissant naïvement' when blaming Oriane, suggesting the criticism may stem from a private grievance rather than a disinterested judgment; this materially affects whether Oriane's diminishment should be read as endorsed or merely reported.
The woman referred to as 'ma cousine Poictiers' does not match any entry on the reference sheet and is treated as a distinct, unresolved named character.
